title: Robustness of DNA looping across multiple cell divisions in individual bacteria.
authors: Chang, Chang; Garcia-Alcala, Mayra; Saiz, Leonor; Vilar, Jose M G; Cluzel, Philippe
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文研究细菌中DNA成环介导的转录抑制鲁棒性，涉及蛋白-DNA互作机制，但以实验和随机模拟为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，且非典型TF-DNA结合位点预测或结构建模。
abstract: DNA looping has emerged as a central paradigm of transcriptional regulation, as it is shared across many living systems. One core property of DNA looping-based regulation is its ability to greatly enhance repression or activation of genes with only a few copies of transcriptional regulators. However, this property based on a small number of proteins raises the question of the robustness of such a mechanism with respect to the large intracellular perturbations taking place during growth and division of the cell. Here we address the issue of sensitivity to variations of intracellular parameters of gene regulation by DNA looping. We use the lac system as a prototype to experimentally identify the key features of the robustness of DNA looping in growing Escherichia coli cells. Surprisingly, we observe time intervals of tight repression spanning across division events, which can sometimes exceed 10 generations. Remarkably, the distribution of such long time intervals exhibits memoryless statistics that is mostly insensitive to repressor concentration, cell division events, and the number of distinct loops accessible to the system. By contrast, gene regulation becomes highly sensitive to these perturbations when DNA looping is absent. Using stochastic simulations, we propose that the observed robustness to division emerges from the competition between fast, multiple rebinding events of repressors and slow initiation rate of the RNA polymerase. We argue that fast rebinding events are a direct consequence of DNA looping that ensures robust gene repression across a range of intracellular perturbations.
abstract_zh: DNA环化（DNA looping）已成为转录调控的核心范式，因其在众多生命系统中普遍存在。基于DNA环化的调控的一个核心特性是，它能够仅凭少数几拷贝的转录调控因子，大幅增强基因的抑制或激活。然而，这种基于少量蛋白质的特性引发了一个问题，即该机制在细胞生长和分裂过程中发生的巨大胞内扰动下是否具有稳健性。在此，我们探讨DNA环化基因调控对胞内参数变化的敏感性问题。我们以lac系统为原型，通过实验识别生长中大肠杆菌（Escherichia coli）细胞内DNA环化稳健性的关键特征。令人惊讶的是，我们观察到跨越分裂事件的紧密抑制时间间隔，有时可超过10代。值得注意的是，这种长时间间隔的分布表现出无记忆统计特性，该特性对阻遏物浓度、细胞分裂事件以及系统可及的独特环化数量大多不敏感。相比之下，当DNA环化缺失时，基因调控对这些扰动变得高度敏感。利用随机模拟，我们提出观察到的对分裂的稳健性源于阻遏物快速多次再结合事件与RNA聚合酶缓慢起始速率之间的竞争。我们认为，快速再结合事件是DNA环化的直接结果，它确保了在多种胞内扰动下基因抑制的稳健性。
